idea.name: Gourmet cupcake bakery started from a cupcake truck (Lancaster Cupcake)
idea.one_liner: Start baking from home, launch with a $1,200 converted cupcake truck at fairs and events, then scale to central production bakery, three retail locations, decorating classes/events and nationwide shipping
idea.customer: local consumers, event-goers, corporate/catering clients, nationwide gift buyers
idea.offer: cupcakes, jar cakes, cakes, ice cream, decorating classes, shipped cupcakes
idea.revenue_model: retail and truck sales (~$3.47 per cupcake, ~$24 average sale), events, shipping/QVC

key_quotes.quote: We started with $1,400, bought some ingredients and we kept moving forward and said, let's bake.
So $1,200 on the purchase of this truck, we fitted out with cabinets inside from myKEA.
Otherwise, you can probably create a social media page and start selling larger, probably, corporate or catering orders.

claims.claim: Cost per cupcake ~$1 all-in vs $3.47 price
claims.quote: And our cost per cupcake is about a dollar all in.

claims.claim: Sold 1,000 cupcakes in one hour on day one
claims.quote: So we sold 1,000 cupcakes in one hour on our first day.
So now we have about 60 employees. Whoa, our labor costs are about 40% of our revenue.
Our marketing, we have more card of our budget, is very small, about 1% of our sales into marketing.
This location, we're spending about $12,000 a month to be here because it's almost two locations.

acquisition_channels.details: truck holds 1,000 cupcakes, often sells out
email/Facebook for sales, Instagram/TikTok for awareness

ideas.delivery: Central production bakery with premixes, depositor (~$20k), ~3,000-6,000 cupcakes/day; Profit First accounting taking 10% off the top
ideas.other_uk_rules: Register food business with local council 28 days before trading; food hygiene rating; street trading licence for truck; Natasha's Law allergen labelling for prepacked foods
